ov: A domesticated South American camelid, used by Andean cultures for meat and as a pack animal since before Columbus. Llamas are social herd animals and are also used as livestock guardians.

why.et: Used for meat and as a pack animal in the Andes since before Columbus.

rg: Domestic, from the Andes of South America.

cf.tip: A llama is bigger than an alpaca, with a longer head and curved, banana-shaped ears. Alpacas are smaller and bred for their finer fibre.

fx: A llama can carry about 25–30% of its body weight for 8–13 km.

_cf.tip: A llama is bigger than an alpaca, with a longer head and curved, banana-shaped ears. Alpacas are smaller and bred for their finer fibre.
A llama is a South American relative of the camel but not a true camel, and it has no hump.
The llama is the domesticated descendant of the guanaco; the guanaco’s colour varies very little.
